tagline: Algeria's northeastern port city on the Gulf of Annaba — a commercial and ferry harbour, the Rizi Amor corniche and the Cap de Garde headland framing a bay that today moves entirely by road.
summary: Annaba (ancient Bône, beside the Roman ruins of Hippo Regius) is Algeria's fourth-largest city and the industrial capital of the country's northeast, fronting the Mediterranean on the wide Gulf of Annaba. It carries a major commercial port — steel from the nearby El Hadjar complex, phosphates and containers — plus a passenger-ferry terminal with seasonal Algérie Ferries service to Marseille. The urban bay strings together the port, the Rizi Amor / Saint-Cloud corniche beaches, the Cap de Garde headland and lighthouse, and the fishing village of Chetaïbi around the western cape, all linked today only by a congested coast road. Demand is commuter-, tourism- and leisure-led: Rabah Bitat (Les Salines) Airport feeds the metro, and the Seraïdi hill resort and beach belt draw heavy summer traffic. A clean foiling-electric layer fits the short intra-bay hops (Pioneer II) between the port, corniche and Cap de Garde, and the coastal run to Chetaïbi, giving Yassir's Algerian home market a credible eastern water node beyond Algiers and Béjaïa.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: All the Annaba legs — port ↔ corniche (~2 nm), Cap de Garde (~5 nm) and the coastal run to Chetaïbi (~22 nm) — sit well inside the ~70 nm all-electric envelope, with shore charging at the port basin supporting frequent rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for Annaba's intra-gulf network; the Quanta-LR range tier is reserved for longer open-sea legs elsewhere on the Algerian coast.

competitive_landscape: Today: a single congested coast road along the corniche, the commercial/ferry port, and seasonal beach shuttles; no clean fast-passenger intra-bay service.
seasonality: Strong summer leisure peak on the corniche and beaches; mild Mediterranean climate year-round for commuter legs.
regulatory_note: Port of Annaba is a commercial + ferry port under ANP; intra-bay leisure boarding points would sit alongside existing harbour operations.
